mainEntity.name: How much does a Ford Fiesta 1.25 & 1.4 Petrol engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost depends on the engine's condition. A used Ford Fiesta 1.25 & 1.4 Petrol engine typically costs £200-£500, while a reconditioned unit ranges from £700-£1,400. A fully rebuilt engine with a warranty costs £1,200-£2,000 (supply only).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Ford Fiesta 1.25 & 1.4 Petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's current market value. If your Ford Fiesta 1.25 & 1.4 Petrol is worth under £2,000, a full rebuilt engine replacement may exceed the car's value, making a used engine or scrap evaluation more sensible. For vehicles valued over £3,000, a reconditioned engine with a warranty is a financially sound investment.

commonProblems.h2: Ford Fiesta 1.25 & 1.4 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Ford Fiesta 1.25 and 1.4 Duratec petrol engines are widely regarded as some of the most reliable naturally aspirated units in the Fiesta lineup. However, high-mileage examples are prone to specific ignition and cooling component wear. The FXJA, FXJB, RTJA, and RTJB codes dominate replacement demand due to cumulative wear on coil packs and water pumps. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Coil Pack Failure & Misfires - Why the Ford Fiesta 1.25 & 1.4 Petrol Loses Power
problems.affectedModels: Ford Fiesta 1.25 & 1.4 Petrol (FXJA, FXJB, RTJA, RTJB, 2008-2017)
problems.rootCause: The ignition coil packs are exposed to high under-bonnet temperatures over time, leading to internal insulation breakdown, misfires, and rough idling.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing faulty coil packs and spark plugs.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly effective if caught early; no internal engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary only if prolonged misfires have caused catastrophic catalytic converter or internal valve damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Ford Fiesta 1.25 & 1.4 Petrol (Mk6/Mk7) is currently valued between £500 and £3,500 depending on year and condition [THIRD-PARTY]. - Vehicle worth under ~£3,000: repair or a used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£3,000-£6,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£6,000+: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. If your Ford Fiesta 1.25 & 1.4 Petrol is valued under £2,000, a full rebuilt engine replacement cost risks exceeding the vehicle's value. Evaluate scrap or part-exchange value first.
problems.recommendation: If the issue is isolated to a misfire, replacing the coil packs and spark plugs is highly cost-effective and usually resolves the problem. However, if the engine has suffered catastrophic internal damage, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine is the most financially sound long-term solution, provided the vehicle's value justifies the investment.

problems.group: Water Pump Leaks & Cooling System Issues
problems.h4: Water Pump Leaks & Cooling System Issues - Why the Ford Fiesta 1.25 & 1.4 Petrol Overheats
problems.affectedModels: Ford Fiesta 1.25 & 1.4 Petrol (FXJA, FXJB, RTJA, RTJB, 2008-2017)
problems.rootCause: The water pump seals degrade over time, leading to coolant leaks. If ignored, this can cause the engine to overheat, potentially warping the cylinder head.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the water pump, thermostat, and coolant flush.
repairOptions.longevity: Essential preventative maintenance; prevents catastrophic overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if overheating has already warped the cylinder head or cracked the block.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a £2,500 Ford Fiesta 1.25 & 1.4 Petrol, a £300 specialist water pump service is highly viable, but a £1,500+ engine replacement requires careful evaluation against the vehicle's current market value. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.
problems.recommendation: Always monitor coolant levels and address minor leaks immediately. If the engine has already overheated significantly, a rebuilt unit is the safest and most reliable path forward.
